headline: Futures point higher (+2.84%), the S&P 500 is 11.6% below its high, this is a correction, the mood is extreme fear.
summary: The index is below its 200-day average, which is when to be most careful. Fear this deep has usually been a better time to buy than to sell, but it can get worse first.

sections.title: What kind of market this is

lines.t: Correction. 10% to 20% below the high. It has been this way for 1 trading day, after a stretch of pullback. From days like this the S&P 500 was higher three months later 74% of the time, averaging +5.8%.
Painful but historically a better time to add than to sell, with big swings on the way.
0 of 5 recession warnings are lit. None of the classic warnings is flashing.
The Fed's interest rate: The Federal Reserve's rate is 3.88%, unchanged from a year ago. The Fed has been holding steady.
Inflation (consumer prices): Prices are up 4.1% from a year ago; a year earlier the figure was 3.0%. The Fed aims for about 2%.
Unemployment rate: 4.1% of people looking for work cannot find it, down 0.30 points from a year ago.
Junk bond spread: Risky companies pay 3.52 points more than the government to borrow, up 0.19 points in a month. Under 5 points means lenders are calm.
Of 6 conditions in place today, 5 have been followed by better-than-usual returns over the next three months and 1 by worse. A typical three months for the S&P 500: +3.8%.
